user.title: Helios Forecast: panel line
user.description: One forecast for a photovoltaic installation. Add a panel line per orientation, several lines share this installation's single production sensor and inverter cap. Leave the location blank to use your Home Assistant home.

data.name: Name (e.g. South roof)
data.azimuth: Azimuth (degrees from north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west)
data.line_inverter_max_kw: Inverter max output for this line (kW, optional)
data.production_entity: PV production energy sensor (kWh, for the learned correction)
data.battery_min_soc: Battery reserve, minimum state of charge (%, default 10)
data.curtailment_entity: Curtailment signal (binary sensor, input boolean or switch, optional)

data_description.production_entity: A cumulative energy sensor (kWh), e.g. your inverter's or energy meter's total production. A power sensor (W) will not work: it has no long-term sum statistics, so the learning and the reliability index would stay off.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Fill in the capacity and this sensor to turn on the battery state-of-charge projection. Home consumption is taken from your Energy dashboard, so it needs no sensor here.
data_description.curtailment_entity: On while your inverter is being held back for a reason the sky cannot explain: a full battery, a zero-export rule, a grid limit. The hours it marks are not learned as low production. Without it, a full battery is still detected from the state of charge sensor and the inverter cap.

benchmark.title: Helios Forecast: community benchmark
benchmark.description:
An open measurement of how accurate Helios Forecast really is, on real installations, published as it goes. Would you like to take part? It happens here: [helios-ha.org/benchmark](https://helios-ha.org/benchmark)

Get a key in one click, with no account and no name, then paste it below. To stop everything, clear it.

data.benchmark_enabled: Contribute to the public accuracy benchmark (optional)

data_description.benchmark_enabled: Sends what this installation predicts, once an hour, so it can be compared with what it really produced. The results are published openly. Only your panel geometry, the predicted curve, the measured production and the reliability index are sent: no entity names, no consumption, no other sensor, and your coordinates rounded to about a kilometre. Off unless you turn it on.
data_description.benchmark_key: The write key you were given when joining the benchmark. Nothing is sent without it.
data_description.benchmark_url: Where the measurements are sent, shown so you know exactly where they go.

get_forecast.name: Get forecast
get_forecast.description: Returns the full production forecast (today onward, one point per 15 minutes, each with the predicted watts and the P10/P90 confidence band) as response data, for use in automations.

config_entry_id.name: Installation
config_entry_id.description: Which Helios Forecast installation to read. Optional when only one is configured.

get_battery_soc_forecast.name: Get battery SoC forecast
get_battery_soc_forecast.description: Returns the projected battery state of charge for the next 48 hours (one point per 15 minutes) as response data, for use in automations.

config_entry_id.name: Installation
config_entry_id.description: Which Helios Forecast installation to read. Optional when only one is configured.

location_invalid.title: Location out of range
location_invalid.description: The location set for {entry} ({latitude}, {longitude}) is not a valid latitude and longitude. Latitude runs from -90 to 90 and longitude from -180 to 180; leave both blank to use the Home Assistant home.

location_far.title: Location far from your Home Assistant home
location_far.description: The location set for {entry} is {km} km from the Home Assistant home. If the installation really is there, ignore this; otherwise check a decimal in the latitude or longitude.

no_lines.title: No panel line
no_lines.description: {entry} has no panel line, so there is nothing to forecast. Add at least one line with its tilt, azimuth and peak power.

line_kwp_missing.title: Panel line {line}: peak power missing
line_kwp_missing.description: Line {line} of {entry} has no peak power, or zero. Without it every figure stays flat. Enter the line's peak power in kWp (for example 3.6 for 3600 Wp).

line_kwp_unit.title: Panel line {line}: peak power looks like watts
line_kwp_unit.description: Line {line} of {entry} declares {kwp} kWp, which is far beyond a home installation. The value was most likely typed in watts. Enter it in kilowatts-peak (for example 4.05 rather than 4050).

line_tilt.title: Panel line {line}: tilt out of range
line_tilt.description: Line {line} of {entry} has a tilt of {tilt} degrees. Tilt runs from 0 (flat) to 90 (vertical).

line_azimuth.title: Panel line {line}: azimuth out of range
line_azimuth.description: Line {line} of {entry} has an azimuth of {azimuth} degrees. Azimuth runs from 0 to 360 clockwise from north: 90 is east, 180 south, 270 west.

line_tracker.title: Panel line {line}: unknown tracker type
line_tracker.description: Line {line} of {entry} declares a tracker of type {tracker}, which this integration does not know. Pick one of the offered types, or none for a fixed array.

line_location_invalid.title: Panel line {line}: coordinates out of range
line_location_invalid.description: Line {line} of {entry} has coordinates that are not a valid latitude and longitude. Correct them or leave both blank to place the line at the installation's location.

line_location_far.title: Panel line {line}: coordinates far from the installation
line_location_far.description: Line {line} of {entry} is placed {km} km from the installation. Panels on a distant field are possible, a wrong decimal is more likely; check the line's latitude and longitude.

line_cap_unit.title: Panel line {line}: inverter limit looks like watts
line_cap_unit.description: Line {line} of {entry} has an inverter limit of {cap} kW for {kwp} kWp of panels. The limit was most likely typed in watts. Enter it in kilowatts.

inverter_cap_unit.title: Inverter limit looks like watts
inverter_cap_unit.description: {entry} has an inverter limit of {cap} kW for {kwp} kWp of panels. The limit was most likely typed in watts. Enter it in kilowatts (for example 5 rather than 5000).

inverter_cap_low.title: Inverter limit well below the panels
inverter_cap_low.description: {entry} has an inverter limit of {cap} kW for {kwp} kWp of panels, so the forecast will be clipped most of the day. If the limit is right, ignore this; otherwise check the value or its unit.

production_entity_unset.title: No production sensor: the forecast cannot learn
production_entity_unset.description: {entry} has no production sensor. The forecast still runs on physics and weather, but nothing corrects it against what your panels really deliver. Pick the cumulative energy sensor (kWh) of your inverter or meter in the settings.

trend_anchor_hour.title: Trend reference hour out of range
trend_anchor_hour.description: {entry} has a trend reference hour of {hour}. Enter a local hour from 0 to 23.

battery_soc_entity_unset.title: Battery: capacity set but no state of charge sensor
battery_soc_entity_unset.description: {entry} declares a battery of {capacity} kWh but no state of charge sensor, so the projection stays off. Pick the battery's state of charge sensor (in %) or clear the capacity.

battery_capacity_unset.title: Battery: state of charge sensor set but no capacity
battery_capacity_unset.description: {entry} names a battery state of charge sensor but no usable capacity, so the projection stays off. Enter the battery's usable capacity in kWh or clear the sensor.

battery_capacity.title: Battery capacity out of range
battery_capacity.description: {entry} declares a battery of {capacity} kWh, which is not a home battery. Enter the usable capacity in kilowatt-hours (for example 10 rather than 10000).

battery_power.title: Battery charge or discharge power implausible
battery_power.description: {entry} declares a battery power of {power} kW for a capacity of {capacity} kWh, more than three times its capacity per hour. Check the value and its unit (kW, not W).

battery_min_soc.title: Battery reserve out of range
battery_min_soc.description: {entry} has a minimum state of charge of {value}. Enter a percentage from 0 to 100.

battery_efficiency.title: Battery efficiency out of range
battery_efficiency.description: {entry} has a round-trip efficiency of {value}. Enter a percentage from 50 to 100 (most home batteries sit around 90).

benchmark_key.title: Benchmark key does not look like a key
benchmark_key.description: {entry} takes part in the community benchmark but its key is not one the collector issues. Paste the whole key from helios-ha.org/benchmark, or switch the benchmark off.

production_entity_missing.title: Production sensor not found
production_entity_missing.description: The production sensor of {entry}, {entity}, does not exist. The forecast runs uncorrected until it does. Check the entity id, or pick the sensor again in the settings.

production_entity_kind.title: Production sensor is not a cumulative energy sensor
production_entity_kind.description: The production sensor of {entry}, {entity}, reports {unit} with state class {state_class}. The learning needs a cumulative energy sensor in kWh (state class total or total_increasing), not a power sensor. Pick your inverter's or meter's energy total; the Integral helper turns a power sensor into one.

battery_soc_entity_missing.title: Battery state of charge sensor not found
battery_soc_entity_missing.description: The battery sensor of {entry}, {entity}, does not exist, so the projection stays off. Check the entity id or pick the sensor again.

battery_soc_entity_unit.title: Battery sensor is not a percentage
battery_soc_entity_unit.description: The battery sensor of {entry}, {entity}, reports {unit}. The projection needs the state of charge in percent.

curtailment_entity_missing.title: Curtailment signal not found
curtailment_entity_missing.description: The curtailment signal of {entry}, {entity}, does not exist. Hours the inverter is held back are then learned as bad sky. Check the entity id or clear the field.

production_history_empty.title: Production sensor has no history yet
production_history_empty.description: {entity}, the production sensor of {entry}, has no long-term statistics yet. The learning starts as soon as the recorder has a few hours; if this persists after a day, the sensor is not a cumulative energy sensor.

production_at_night.title: Production sensor counts at night
production_at_night.description: {entity}, the production sensor of {entry}, recorded {kwh} kWh while the sun was well below the horizon. Panels make nothing at night, so this sensor measures more than the panels (a grid or house meter). Pick the sensor that counts the inverter's output only.

production_above_panels.title: Production above what the declared panels can deliver
production_above_panels.description: {entity}, the production sensor of {entry}, reached {kw} kW several times for {kwp} kWp of declared panels. Either the peak power is too small, or the sensor counts more than the panels. Check both.

production_stale.title: No production recorded for {days} days
production_stale.description: {entity}, the production sensor of {entry}, has not increased for {days} days. Snow or an outage can explain it; if the panels do produce, the sensor stopped reporting and the learning is starving.

consumption_source_sparse.title: Consumption source {source} reports intermittently
consumption_source_sparse.description: In the Energy dashboard, {source} has data for {pct}% of the hours the best source covers ({best}%). The consumption profile is built only from the hours it does cover, so it stays right but rests on less history. A more reliable sensor for that flow makes the battery projection sharper.

benchmark_excluded.title: Kept out of the benchmark figures ({reason})
benchmark_excluded.description: The community benchmark received the emissions of {entry} but keeps them out of the published figures. Reason {reason}: kwp means the declared peak power is missing, zero or typed in watts; night means the production sensor records energy at night, so it measures more than the panels. Correct the configuration and the installation is counted again within a day.
